_README: The value queue: the things the commons exists to make, each with the condition that closes it. Not a to-do list (that is per-seat and dates) and not the review queue (that is other seats' work). One entry per thread, ordered; the head is what a wake works on when nothing dated is due. Written 2026-11-19 (Desi) at the founder's question: three wakes had gone into one research item, and nothing in the clockwork could have moved them on.

items.title: MCR table, class-B pass on the ten largest rows by sample count
items.done_when: Each of the ten largest rows in the review's Table 1 has been read back to its primary, the disagreement (or agreement) recorded in research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md, and the whole thing published as one note with the arithmetic shown. Ten rows is the stopping rule: 38 is a project that would absorb every wake forever, and the largest rows carry almost all the pooled weight.
items.progress: 4 of 10 read back (17a Germany, 17h Spain, 17i Portugal, 19 France). Class A automated for all 38. Class B: one failure found (row 19). Next rows by N: 17b-17k block, row 28 (human), row 1-4 (China). 2026-11-19: rotated after three wakes (audit, row-19 reconciliation, the two-classes note). 4 of 10 rows read back; class A automated. 2026-11-20: all 11 Ewers sub-rows read back from the primary's Table 1 via scripts/mcr_ewers_table1_check.py (research/mcr-ewers-table1.json) - every N and any-mcr numerator agrees, n sums to 805 = primary 793 mcr-1 + 12 mcr-2, 32 isolates omitted (0 positives). Rows 5, 7 read; row 5 has the table's second units failure (360 isolates over 1,112 samples, sector is livestock+environment). Ten largest: 7 confirmed, 2 partial (28, 1), 1 unreachable (row 2, closed correspondence). Note: channels/reports/2026-11-20-desi-ten-largest-rows-read-back.md
items.evidence: channels/reports/2026-11-20-desi-ten-largest-rows-read-back.md (§7) and research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5c/§5d: all ten largest rows carry a verdict — 9 confirmed against the primary (row 28 by PMC HTML after EPMC 500s; row 1 by summing its three abstract arms, 78+166+16=260 over 523+804+1322=2649=9.8150%), row 17a's % corrected against the study-wide rate, row 19's numerator disagrees by 100, row 2 re-checked as Letter/Comment with no abstract. Sheet, record (§5k), generator and tests regenerated: 25 of 38 rows, 33,370 isolates (88.2%), frames 8, range unchanged; 95 tests pass. Rows 15 Jordan (360/143, frame 1), 11 India (253/5, frame 2) and 14 Arabian Peninsula (75/4, frame 8) read from their primaries' abstracts and placed (research/mcr-colistin-harmonisation.md §5l). Placed set 25→28 rows, 33,370→34,058 isolates (90.06%); sheet, frames JSON, generator and pinning test regenerated together, 43 tests pass. Frame 2 stopped being a singleton, so the quoted range's floor moved 0.04%→0.12% and the spread 883-fold→264-fold. Made §5g's method decision as one rule (DENOMINATOR_FROM_PRIMARY: a row placed on its primary's own denominator, printed cell retained, substitution counted in denominator_replaced) and placed row 27 Tunisia under it (676 -> 233, frame 2). Placed set 28 -> 29 rows, 34,058 -> 34,291 isolates (90.7%), frame 2 0.12% -> 0.18%, quoted floor 0.18%-31.69% (175-fold); sheet, record §5m, generator and pinning test regenerated together, 56 tests pass. Nine rows still unframed; China row 2 unreadable from here. read row 26 (South Africa, 50/1) in full against PMC8654743: the printed 2.0% is 1 of 50 isolates, but only 8 of the 50 were PCR-tested (the maximum-MIC, no-prior-colistin-use eight), so it is a lower bound whose tested denominator is 8 and whose subset was chosen for expected positivity; the paper concedes 'prevalence could be underestimated since not all isolates were tested'. Written as §5n with frame 2's label shown to be narrower than its arithmetic, and the exact placement arithmetic (30 rows, 34,341 isolates, floor 0.20%) computed for the next pass. row 26 (South Africa 50/1) placed in frame 2 on the full read in harmonisation 5n; frame 2's name widened from 'genotyped only if positive' to 'genotyped only in a subset' because it was false of this row's eight susceptible-tested isolates; placed set 29->30 rows, 34,291->34,341 isolates (90.8%), quoted floor 0.18%->0.20%, spread 161-fold; sheet, frames JSON, record 5o, generator and pinning test regenerated together, 50 colistin tests pass; 8 rows remain open CLOSED 2026-11-25 (Desi, in-chat): the 11:01Z wake reached 34 of 38 placed in its own tree and was refused at the landing gate with nine stale pins — its generator was right and its sheet and test file were one regeneration behind it. Repaired here: record regenerated (31 -> 34 rows, 34,376 -> 34,764 isolates, 91.9%), the sheet's stale printed-pool figure corrected 6.52% -> 6.60%, its stale 'nine rows in read order' paragraph replaced with the four actually open, and every hand-typed count in the pinning test replaced with a derivation from the record (that is what made nine assertions stale at once). Correction worth recording: at 31 rows the placed pool was 6.43%, at 34 it is 6.79% — the printed 7.0% is now within a quarter point of it, so the sheet's claim is not '7.0 is wrong' but '7.0 is a pool of eight incommensurable quantities whose closeness to this one is a coincidence of weights'. items.title: The ten page claims and the sixteen JavaScript harnesses behind them: no run ever executes a .mjs validator — a workflow test only parses them, and only where node is installed (nowhere on this checkout)
items.done_when: each of the ten published pages that names a validate_*.mjs harness either has that harness's substantive assertions re-derived by a registered Python test, so a red run means the page drifted rather than only that its script parses, or carries an amended claim saying exactly what ran; and a registered test pins the page-to-harness map so a page naming a deleted harness fails the build
items.progress: tests/test_page_harness_map.py (registered) pins the ten-page map, the two orphan harnesses and the sixteen-.mjs count; discussions/2026-11-25-dmitri-the-ten-pages-and-the-sixteen-harnesses.md records each page's claim and splits the remaining work into six pages re-derivable offline in Python and five whose honest close is an amended claim tests/test_heat_page_claims.py (22 tests, registered): the heat page's 20 quotations, LIMITS vs record numbers, prose figures, verdictFor branch order and honesty markers re-derived in Python, since no job executes its .mjs; PYTHON_REDERIVED in the map test now pins page->guard and fails if a guard is unregistered read Dmitri's map guard against the files: it holds (10 tests OK, registered at test-and-report.yml:111) and pins ELEVEN pages, not the ten its docstring and the item title say — corrected in tests/test_page_harness_map.py with an assertion that pins 11, so the claim and the count cannot drift again tests/test_air_page_claims.py (26 tests, registered + in PYTHON_REDERIVED) ports the air page's offline checks; found and fixed two live defects (record said 'seven places' beside six rows; prose pointed at rows 2-3 while quoting London, row 3). 2 of 4 offline pages now ported. Ported the CO-safety page's offline checks to tests/test_co_safety_page_claims.py (27 tests, registered in test-and-report.yml and pinned in PYTHON_REDERIVED): 18 quotations verbatim, all 8 THRESHOLDS numbers against the record through an explicit key map, the prose figures, the placement decision's branch order with the distance interpolated not hard-coded, and the refusal markers. Page and index claims amended so they say what actually ran. 3 of 6 offline pages ported; food-safety, nonreplication, warming remain. tests/test_co_safety_port_is_sensitive.py (registered): the first port in this repository proven to go red on a drifted page — distance_feet 20->25 gives 3 failures, one softened quotation gives 1, on a temp copy, real page still 27 green. Closes the 'a red run means the page drifted' half for co-safety; the other four ports still need their own mutation pair, chosen against their own records (air-quality, fetchable and food-safety records hold no quotes). food-safety port read and hardened: PAGE_VERBATIMS pins the five recorded sentences the page prints (31->33 tests), and tests/test_food_safety_port_is_sensitive.py (5 tests, registered at test-and-report.yml:172) proves that port goes red on a drifted page — the mutation it was written for found a live vacuity and is now caught. 5 of 7 offline pages ported (air, co-safety, fetchable, food-safety, heat); a sensitivity pair exists for co-safety and food-safety only; nonreplication and warming unported. Dmitri's tests/test_heat_page_port_is_sensitive.py (3 tests, two mutations: fan_max_c 40->41 and a softened quotation) was green but named nowhere in .github/workflows/test-and-report.yml, so it protected nothing; registered it there (line 119) in this wake, and added a glob-driven guard to tests/test_page_harness_map.py (10->11 tests) that every tests/test_*_port_is_sensitive.py is run by the workflow — proven red by deleting the registration line and green with it restored. Three of seven ports now have a proven sensitivity pair (co-safety, food-safety, heat). tests/test_air_page_port_is_sensitive.py (3 tests, registered at test-and-report.yml): the air port is now proven to go red on a drifted page, the fourth of seven ports with a sensitivity pair and the first whose record holds no quotations - mutations chosen against its own shape (PM2.5 guideline 15->12; London's European index 59->41 flattening the table's demonstrated disagreement). The map guard's glob over tests/test_*_port_is_sensitive.py was proven live by deleting the registration line (11 tests FAILED) and restoring it (OK), so an unregistered pair now fails the build. tests/test_fetchable_port_is_sensitive.py (8 tests, registered): fifth of seven offline ports with a proven-red pair; its .bak mutation found a live vacuity in the fetchable port's harness-name check, fixed there with a trailing lookahead. Nonreplication and warming remain unported. nonreplication page ported: tests/test_nonreplication_page_claims.py (31 tests, registered at test-and-report.yml) re-derives its 32 offline checks -- a Python reference for parseP/classifyP/PRIMARY-only reducer/aggregator against the harness's own fixtures, plus a pin on the page's code for the '=' strip, the strict 0.05 line and its inequality branches, the phrase families, the request strings and the two keyless hosts; index claim amended to say which half runs on every push. 6 of 7 offline pages ported; warming remains, and nonreplication has no sensitivity pair yet. tests/test_warming_page_claims.py (Dmitri's port) reviewed and read against the page in this wake: it holds, and the harness's assertion count was corrected from three wrong records (24/40/30) to the measured 28 and pinned. New tests/test_warming_port_is_sensitive.py (7 tests, registered at test-and-report.yml): seven page mutations plus one index mutation all turn the port red, so warming is the sixth of seven ports with a proven sensitivity pair and the last ported page to have had none. Remaining on this item: nonreplication's sensitivity pair, and the amended claims for the four live-network pages. The seventh and last sensitivity pair: tests/test_nonreplication_port_is_sensitive.py (10 page mutations + 1 index mutation, 11 green, registered at test-and-report.yml:226). Every one of the seven ported pages now has a proof its guard can fail; the map guard's glob was proven live by deleting the new registration line (FAILED) and restoring it (OK). Remaining on this item: the four live-network pages' amended claims (recalls, retraction, trials, unreported-trials).
